rows.speaker: الشيخ سعيد
rows.claim: The poem says the path of purity reaches its destination only by following Mustafa.
rows.anchor: مندار سعدى كه راه صفا توان رفت جزبرى مصطفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philosophers, Brahmins, and monks falsely claimed that reason, ascetic discipline, and struggle could reach God without prophets or divine guidance, so they failed to arrive.
rows.anchor: الفلاسفة والبراهمة والرهابنة ادعوا معرفة الله والوصول إليه بطريق العقل والرياضة والمجاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the Prophet's blessing includes exalting religion, joining sovereignty to prophethood, and granting him other religious and worldly favors.
rows.anchor: بإعلاء الدين وضم الملك إلى النبوة وغيرهما مما أفاضه عليه من النعم الدينية والدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path concerns conveying the message and establishing leadership; its basis already existed, but the conquest clarified truth's routes and made its methods straighter.
rows.anchor: في تبليغ الرسالة وإقامة مراسم الرياسة وأصل الاستقامة وإن كانت حاصلة قبل الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit divine name at the verse's close marks the ultimate end and highlights special care for the victory, reinforced by the phrase “mighty victory.”
rows.anchor: إظهار الاسم الجليل لكونه خاتمة الغايات ولإظهار كمال العناية بشأن النصر

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: A mighty victory includes defeating and prevailing over the enemy; a less mighty victory provides protection and merely repels the enemy.
rows.anchor: النصر العزيز هو الذي معه غلبة العدو والظهور عليه والنصر غير العزيز هو الذي معه الحماية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading makes “mighty” mean strong and impregnable, describing victory by the quality of its recipient, the one made victorious, for emphasis.
rows.anchor: نصرا قويا منيعا على وصف المصدر بوصف صاحبه أي المنصور مجازا للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows “a victory whose possessor is mighty” as a possible construction for the phrase.
rows.anchor: أو نصرا عزيزا صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing victory by the quality of the One who grants it adds little, since the passage describes the addressee's state rather than the speaker's.
rows.anchor: ولم يجعل وصفا بوصف الناصر لقلة الفائدة فيه لأن القصد بيان حال المخاطب لا المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory chiefly means the gains following the conquest of Mecca, including victory over Hawazin and later Muslim victories over the Persians and Byzantines.
rows.anchor: المراد من ذلك النصر هو ما ترتب على فتح مكة من النصر على الأعداء كهوازن وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some messengers fought because opponents' rejection of innate monotheism corrupted their primordial nature through deeds that disrupted the order they were charged to preserve; a prophet remains a mercy even when sent with the sword.
rows.anchor: مخالفة ما فطروا عليه من التوحيد الموجبة تلك المخالفة لفساد ذلك الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same rationale applies to anyone who undertakes commanding right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: وقس عليه سائر من تصدى للأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ maps the surah's gifts in order: conquest signals answered prayer, forgiveness love, completed blessing election, guidance realization of truth, and victory sainthood.
rows.anchor: جمع الله لنبيه في هذه السورة نعما مختلفة من الفتح المبين وهو من أعلام الإجابة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: He interprets forgiveness as clearing faults, completion as reaching the full degree, guidance as invitation to witnessing, and victory as seeing everything from God without turning to anything else.
rows.anchor: فالمغفرة تبرئة من العيوب وإتمام النعمة إبلاغ الدرجة الكاملة والهداية هي الدعوة إلى المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent tranquility into believers' hearts through the truce and safety after fear: they were few as pilgrims while a stronger, battle-ready enemy faced them, yet they stood firm and pledged to die.
rows.anchor: بسبب الصلح والأمن بعد الخوف لأنهم كانوا قليلي العدة بسبب أنهم معتمرون وكان العدو مستعدين لقتالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's sequence moves from winds to rain clouds, ships on water, and earth under angelic governance, showing effects descend from above; resurrection from graves is likewise possible for the One who causes earthly effects through heavenly powers.
rows.anchor: سر الترتيب هو أن الرياح فوق السحاب الحاملة للمطر وهي فوق الماء الحامل للسفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an inward reading, descending angels visit people of spiritual union and tend to their affairs; those people ask the angels about their absent companions and their state of separation or union.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة المقربين لتفقد أهل الوصلة والقيام بأنواع من الأمور لأهل هذه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of union voice their longing by asking two companions to stop and tell them about their condition.
rows.anchor: بربكما يا صاحبي قفاليا اسائلكما عن حالكم فاسألانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer means that what people are promised—resurrection and reckoning, or reward and punishment—is certainly true; the relative pronoun has an omitted antecedent.
rows.anchor: جواب للقسم وما موصولة والعائد محذوف أي إن الذي توعدونه من البعث والحساب

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Calling a promise “truthful” is like calling a life “pleasing”: the active participle is applied to its object, since a promise is believed true and a life is pleasing.
rows.anchor: ووصف الوعد بالصدق كوصف العيشة بالرضى في أن اسم الفاعل مسند إلى المفعول به

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh reads “truthful” as a relation adjective meaning “possessing truth,” since the promised thing cannot itself be the truthful speaker; the promise is truthful.
rows.anchor: أي لذو صدق على أن البناء للنسب كتامر لأن الموعود لا يكون صادقا بل الصادق هو الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle may be a verbal noun, and “you are promised” may mean either promise or threat; the threat reading better fits the address to deniers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ما مصدرية أي وعدكم أو وعيدكم إذ يحتمل توعدون أن يكون مضارع وعد وأوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “the religion” means recompense for deeds, which will inevitably occur; the One capable of extraordinary creations contrary to nature can also resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: أي وإن الجزاء على الأعمال الحاصل وكائن لا محالة فإن من قدر على هذه الأمور البديعة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: God promises the obedient paradise, penitents love, saints nearness, knowers union, and seekers finding Him; He threatens transgressors with punishment, persistent sinners with hatred, enemies with distance, heedless people with separation, and idle people with loss.
rows.anchor: وعد الله المطيعين بالجنة والتائبين بالمحبة والأولياء بالقربة والعارفين بالوصلة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One asks why an oath is needed: believers accept a plain report and disbelievers gain nothing from an oath; the answer is that the Quran follows Arab custom of swearing to emphasize a matter.
rows.anchor: ما الحكمة في معنى القسم منفإنه إن كان لأجل المؤمن فالمؤمن يصدق بمجرد الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment is established either by testimony or by oath, so God mentions both forms in scripture to leave people no excuse; an oath is made only by something revered.
rows.anchor: والحكم يفصل باثنين إما بالشهادة وإما بالقسم فذكر الله في كتابه النوعين حتى لا يبقى لهم حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by Himself in seven Quranic passages and elsewhere by created things, including the objects named in several surah openings.
rows.anchor: وقد أقسم الله بنفسه في القرآن في سبعة مواضع والباقي من القسم القرآني قسم بمخلوقاته

rows.speaker: ترجمة الفتوحات
rows.claim: The cited warning forbids swearing by a religion other than Islam or saying one would renounce Islam if something were true, and advises renewing faith as a precaution.
rows.anchor: حذركن كه بغير دين إسلام بديني دير سوكند يادكنى ياكويى اكر نين باشد از دين اسلام بيزارم

rows.speaker: مولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jāmī mocks ignorant people who give a ruined thing the name of prosperity, like a child mistaking a swelling for fat.
rows.anchor: مرد جاهل جاه كيتى را لقب دولت نهد همنان آماس بيند طفل كويد فربهست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A satirical poem says the people of the age look human but act like predators, like wolves in clothing or clothing made of wolves.
rows.anchor: شكل ايشان شكل إنسان فعل شان فعل سباع هم ذئبا في ثياب أو ثياب في ذئاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “you named them” refers to the names, not the idols: the people made empty names rather than giving names to real deities, since these idols have no referents.
rows.anchor: ضميرها لها لا للأصنام والمعنى جعلتموها أسماء لا جعلتم لها أسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses what the idolaters desire as what their evil-commanding selves covet, while also saying their ancestors fixed the names according to false whims.
rows.anchor: تشتهيه أنفسهم الأمارة بالسوء فما موصولة ويجوز كونها مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denied “authority” is proof for the validity of calling the idols gods; no such proof was revealed.
rows.anchor: أي بصحة تسميتها {من سلطان} برهان تتعلقون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to third person signals turning away from the idolaters to recount their offenses to others; their naming and worship rest on deluded conjecture and desire.
rows.anchor: التفات إلى الغيبة للإيذان بأن تعداد قبائحهم اقتضى الإعراض عنهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The idols are only imagined forms without real referents, invented by sensual selves and weak, illusion-clouded minds; seekers and people of unveiling recognize them as nonexistent, mere propped-up wood.
rows.anchor: نفوسكم الدنية الشهوانية وجهالة عقولكم السخيفة الهيولانية إلا أسماء صور وهمية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Created things have no independent power to create or destroy, dominate or show gentleness, benefit or harm; all beings are manifestations of divine names and loci of divine attributes of beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: والأشياء علويها وسفليها جمادها ونباتها حيوانها وإنسانها كلها مظاهر الأسماء الإلهية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Truth manifests in each thing according to its capacity, but in the Perfect Human it manifests in its totality, making that human God's vicegerent on earth.
rows.anchor: إلا الإنسان الكامل فإنه تجلى فيه بحسب الكلية المجموعية وصار خليفة الله في الأرض

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The idolaters fail to perceive spiritual realities and divine attributes in creation, turning instead to animal desire and bodily darkness, corrupt conjecture, and ego's preference over God's pleasure; this is manifest loss.
rows.anchor: أعرضتم باتباع الهوات الحيوانية وملازمة الجسمانية الظلمانية عن إدراك تلك اللطائف الروحانية

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says he saw seventy knowers ruined by imagining that they had truly known God; every person's grasp is limited by capacity, while God's majesty exceeds it.
rows.anchor: رأيت سبعين عارفا قد هلكوا بالتوهم أي توهموا أنهم عرفوه تعالى

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says all knowers died in delusion, even Abū Yazīd, who also died imagining he had known God.
rows.anchor: كلهم ماتوا على التوهم حتى أبو يزيد مات على التوهم

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqlī warns that the spiritually conceited mistake mental images and fantasies for unveilings, insights, the unseen realm, or lights of divine power, though they are egoistic and satanic imaginings.
rows.anchor: من الأشكال والمخاييل التي تبدو في غواشي أدمغتهم وهم يحسبون أنها مكاشفات الغيوب

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: He says the Real is beyond shapes and images and warns against keeping company with ignorant claimants to seeing God; true vision belongs to saints, not enemies.
rows.anchor: والحق منزه عن الأشكال والتمثال إياك يا صاحبي وصحبة الجاهلين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about guidance is either circumstantial or parenthetical; in either case it reinforces the falsity of conjecture and makes following it worse for people already reached by revelation.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل يتبعون أو اعتراض وأيا ما كان ففيه تأكيد لبطلان اتباع الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance is the Quran and the Messenger, yet they did not follow either.
rows.anchor: فالهدى القرآن والرسول ولم يهتدوا بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an inward reading, they ruined their uncreated innate readiness by adopting animal and elemental traits and natural darkness; despite the Prophet, Quran, miracles, and signs proving his mission, they followed desire and turned from God and His saint.
rows.anchor: إفساد استعدادهم الفطري الغير المجعول بواسطة تلبسهم بملابس الصفات الحيوانية العنصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance was granted in earthly life, not in pre-eternity; whoever lacked God's light in pre-eternity will have no light forever.
rows.anchor: لأن هداهم ما اءهم إلا في يوم الدنيا لا في يوم الأزل ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called the Bride of the Quran; the source gives differing reports about whether it is Meccan or Medinan and about its verse count.
rows.anchor: وتسمى عروس القرآن مكية أو مدنية وآيها ست أو سبع أو ثمان وسبعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The All-Merciful” begins the sentence and means the One whose mercy is complete; worldly provision is general, while forgiveness in the afterlife is granted to believers.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ما بعده أي الذي له الرحمة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian poem depicts the earth as God's common table, where friend and enemy alike share its bounty.
rows.anchor: أديم زمين سفره عام اوست برين خوان يغما ه دشمن ه دوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy in creatures is affection or spiritual inclination, named by analogy with the womb's physical bending over what it carries; for God it means willing good or bestowing favor.
rows.anchor: وأريد بها بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى إرادة الخير أو الإنعام

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī describes the Merciful as caring for servants through creation, guidance to faith and happiness, their afterlife joy, and the gift of seeing the divine face.
rows.anchor: الرحمن هو العطوف على العباد بالإيجاد أولا وبالهداية إلى الإيمان وأسباب السعادة ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the surah counts worldly and otherworldly, bodily and spiritual blessings, it opens with the name Rahman, the name of the essence encompassing all names and attributes, to ascribe those gifts to Him.
rows.anchor: شاملة لتعداد النعم الدنيوية والأخروية والجسمانية والروحانية طرزها بطراز اسم الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is the greatest blessing and the basis of all happiness; the cited saying calls Quran-bearers the community's noblest, meaning those who regularly recite it and keep night vigils.
rows.anchor: لأنه مدار جميع السعادات ولذا قال عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also says the best people learn the Quran and teach it; it contains the realities of all heavenly scriptures, and its teaching flows from broad divine mercy.
rows.anchor: خيركم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه وفيه جميع حقائق الكتب السماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught Muhammad the Quran through Gabriel, and Muhammad in turn teaches the community.
rows.anchor: بواسطة جبريل عليه السلام وبواسطة محمد عليه السلام غيره من الأمة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī paraphrases the teaching as making learning easy for Muhammad and enabling him to teach others.
rows.anchor: يعني آسان كردانيده مراورا آموختن وديكر انرا آموزانيدن

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: As God taught Adam the names and distinguished him by them, He specially distinguished Muhammad's community by teaching it the Quran and elevating it above other nations; He taught it in pre-eternity and manifested the teaching at creation.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يخص أمة محمد بخاصة مثله

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Although Gabriel mediates Quran teaching outwardly, it is direct without mediation in the inward, special sense.
rows.anchor: من الوجه العام لكنه كان بلا واسطة في المعنى من الوجه الخاص

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: God granted complete readiness to receptive people in pre-eternity; Quran names speech in its unified origin, whereas Furqan names its differentiated end, so Quran teaching does not depend on human creation, but expressive speech does.
rows.anchor: الكلام الإلهي قرآن باعتبار الجمع والبداية وفرقان باعتبار الفرق والنهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order follows this distinction: Quran teaching precedes human creation, while creating the human precedes teaching expression.
rows.anchor: ولذا قدم تعليم القرآن على خلق الإنسان وخلقه على تعليم البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching and making learning easy come from God, not independently from teachers or memorizers; scripture likewise attributes Adam's names, David's armor-making, Jesus's learning, and the hidden knowledge given to al-Khiḍr to God.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن التعليم والتسهيل إنما هو من الله تعالى لا من المعلمين والحافظين

rows.speaker: المشايخ
rows.claim: The shaykhs differ over whether the omen-reader is an unbeliever; the apparent reason for declaring disbelief is that he claimed knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: اختلف المشايخ في كفره وجه الكفر ظاهر لأنه ادعى الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People take the calls of certain birds, such as the owl, as bad omens; believing the birds cause events is disbelief, but mere pessimism is not, especially when treated as inference from signs.
rows.anchor: فإن يكن هناك اعتقاد التأثير منها فذلك كفر وإلا فمجرد التشاؤم لا يوجب الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer should interpret such signs as divine reminders, not certain knowledge of decrees, since God gives life and death, wakes and puts to sleep, through causes and without them.
rows.anchor: والأليق بحال المؤمن حمل مثل ذلك على التنبيهات الإلهية فإنفي كل شيء حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If only” is an urging particle that exposes human inability; the throat is the passage for food, though Kashf al-Asrār calls it the passage for breath and distinguishes it from the food passage.
rows.anchor: لولا للتحضيض لإظهار عجزهم وإذا ظرفية والحلقوم مجرى الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul or spirit is left implicit: the verse means when a person's soul reaches the throat and begins to depart.
rows.anchor: أي الروح أو نفس أحدكم وروحه الحلقوم وتداعت إلى الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says helpers of the Angel of Death cut the veins and gather the spirit little by little until it reaches the throat, where the Angel of Death takes it.
rows.anchor: أن ملك الموت له أعوان يقطعون العروق ويجمعون الروح شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial “while you” addresses those gathered around the dying person, watching the death throes with compassion and a strong wish to rescue the sufferer.
rows.anchor: أي والحال أنتم أيها الحاضرون حول صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to the dying person through knowledge, power, and control, or through the angels who take the soul; observers see only outward signs, cannot grasp the state or its causes, and cannot relieve it.
rows.anchor: أي إلى المحتضر علما وقدرة وتصرفا

rows.speaker: حواشي سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: The preferred explanation is that observers fail to perceive that God knows the dying person better than they do; “seeing” here means insight, not eyesight.
rows.anchor: لا تدركون كوننا أعلم به منكم

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Baqli distinguishes divine nearness by knowledge, encompassing presence, action, attribute, mastery, and gentleness; spatial nearness is impossible for God, while His majesty or beauty is disclosed to hearts of awe or election, and only the near perceive it.
rows.anchor: قرب بالعلم وقرب بالإحاطة وقرب بالفعل وقرب بالصفة وقرب بالقهر وقرب باللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address warns and terrifies its hearers.
rows.anchor: وفي الخطاب تحذير وترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Not under judgment” may mean not owned, enslaved, and humbled; alternatively, it means not recompensed, as in the lexicon al-Mufradāt.
rows.anchor: أي غير مربوبين مملوكين أذلاء من دان السلطان رعيته

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt also explains the word as “not recompensed,” since dīn can mean recompense.
rows.anchor: أو غير مجزيين فإن الدين الجزاء أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return it” means restore the soul to its abode and return the dead person's spirit to the body; the repeated challenge intensifies the conditional proof that they cannot do so.
rows.anchor: أي النفس إلى مقرها وتردون روح ميتكم إلى بدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they deny being created and controlled, they should return the soul at the throat if truthful; their inability proves that God alone controls the matter, so they should believe.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم يمكنكم ذلك فاعلموا أنا لأمر إلى غيركم وهو الله تعالى فآمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final “if you are truthful” repeats the emphasis and does not introduce another conditional challenge, which would make no sense here.
rows.anchor: وهو تكرير للتأكيد لا من اعتراض الشرط إذ لا معنى له هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “brought near” are near in rank to the Throne, not near to God by direction as the Hashwiyya claim; the passage now describes the dead person's postmortem state.
rows.anchor: هو قرب درجاتهم من العرش لا من الله من حيث الجهة حسبما قال به الحشوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brought-near are the most excellent of the three groups, and “rest” can mean relief, mercy by metaphor, or everlasting life without death.
rows.anchor: أي فله استراحة وقرىء بضم الراء وفسر بالرحمة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: “Spirit” has several senses: the soul taken at death; Gabriel, who brings life to hearts; Jesus, whose birth through Gabriel's breath is honorifically attributed to God; divine speech, which revives people from ignorance and unbelief; mercy; and provision that sustains bodies.
rows.anchor: فالروح روح الأجسام الذي يقبض عند الممات وفيه حياة النفس والروح جبرائيل لأنه كان يأتي الأنبياء

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs distinguishes spirit as life or what has life, while the vocalized form with fatḥa can mean relief, mercy, breeze, or a pleasant fragrance.
rows.anchor: الروح بالضم ما فيه الروح ما به حياة الأنفس وبالفتح الراحة والرحمة ونسيم الريح

rows.speaker: كتاب الملل والنحل
rows.claim: The Book of Religions and Sects distinguishes the vocalized forms of rūḥānī and relates spirit as a substance to its characteristic state.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب الملل والنحل الروحاني بالضم من الروح والروحاني بالفتح من الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Basil” may mean provision or fragrant scent; Abū al-ʿĀliya says a person among the brought-near is shown some basil of paradise to smell before death, while al-Zajjāj takes it as paradise's greeting.
rows.anchor: أو هو ما يشم وعن أبي العالية لا يفارق أحد من المقربين الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “He” normally refers to a singular masculine absent, but can refer to God, who is beyond gender; grammarians may treat it as a singular without grammatical or real femininity.
rows.anchor: هو في أصل وضعه كناية عن المفرد المذكر الغائب وهي كناية عن المفردة المؤنثة الغائبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase allows three parses: “He” as subject and Allah as predicate; Allah as apposition with the relative clause as predicate; or “He” as a matter-introducing pronoun, with Allah and the relative clause forming its sentence.
rows.anchor: وهو مبتدأ خبره لفظة الله بمعنى هو المعبود بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Allah the true object of worship and the bearer of the greatest name avoids a tautological equation of “He” and “Allah.”
rows.anchor: فلا يلزم أن يتحد المبتدأ والخبر بأن يكون التقدير الله الله إذ لا فائدة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negating lā comprehensively denies every member of the category; “god” must mean a true object of worship, since false objects of worship do exist and their denial alone would not establish true monotheism.
rows.anchor: ولا في كلمة التوحيد لنفي أفراد الجنس على الشمول والاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be nominative by apposition to the negated term's syntactic position or to the pronoun in an implicit predicate; estimating “existing,” “possible,” or “for us” each creates a different theological confusion.
rows.anchor: وإلا هو مرفوع على البدلية من محل المنفي أو من ضمير الخبر المقدر للا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those confusions disappear when “god” means the One truly worthy of worship: He alone is Lord of the worlds and deserving of accountable creatures' worship.
rows.anchor: والجواب أنه إذا كان المراد بالإله المعبود بالحق كما ذكر فهو لا يكون إلا رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks whether intending the negation to include God makes the exception false, or intending only others makes the exception unnecessary; the answer begins that the heart intends the latter while the wording first appears general.
rows.anchor: إن أراد القائل لا إله إلا الله شمول النفي له تعالى ولغيره فهو مشكل

rows.speaker: جامي
rows.claim: A Persian poem presents each particle as testimony to divine unity and urges Jamī to clear the heart's tablet of duality: God is one, not two.
rows.anchor: لوح خاطر كه حق يكيست نه دو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “knower of unseen and witnessed” is comprehensive: God knows every unseen and witnessed thing, including what escapes senses and intellect and what they perceive, as well as secret and public and this life and the next.
rows.anchor: اللام للاستغراق فيعلم كل غيب وكل شهادة أي ما غاب عن الحسن من الجواهر القدسية

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines the unseen as what is absent from people's senses and insight and the witnessed as what they perceive; he divides known things into four possible or impossible states of existence and says God knows them all.
rows.anchor: ما غاب عن حواس الناس وبصائرهم وما شهدوه بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen precedes the witnessed because it comes first in existence and God's eternal knowledge attaches to it as existent.
rows.anchor: وقدم الغيب على الشهادة لتقدمه في الوجود وتعلق العلم القديم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any ascription of knowledge of the unseen to God describes what is unseen relative to us, since nothing in heaven or earth is hidden from Him; in the pure divine essence all relations fall away, including the relation of knowledge to an unseen object.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ما ورد من إسناد علم الغيب إلى الله فهو الغيب بالنسبة إلينا لا بالنسبة إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated “He” marks the exalted station of these names: whoever occupies himself with them prospers, while whoever turns away perishes.
rows.anchor: من اشتغل به ملك من أعرض عنه هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's worldly mercy reaches every human and jinn, believer and unbeliever; the cited saying contrasts this world's shared provisions with the just judgment of the promised afterlife.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى رحمته الدنيوية عامة لكل إنسي وجني مؤمنا كان أو كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic saying calls people to belong to the afterlife rather than this world, since each mother is followed by her child.
rows.anchor: كونوا من أبناء الآخرة ولا تكونوا من أبناء الدنيا فإن كل أم يتبعها ولدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is called Merciful of this world because its name has an extra letter and its mercy reaches more recipients; He is called Compassionate of the afterlife because that mercy is reserved for believers, with Rahman broader in recipients but fewer kinds or instances of mercy.
rows.anchor: ولذلك يقال يا رحمن الدنيا لأن ما فيه زيادة حرف يراد به زيادة في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing the two names announces that mercy precedes wrath, reassures sinners against despair, and encourages the obedient because God accepts little and gives abundantly.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على سبق رحمته وتبشير للعاصين أن لا يقنطوا من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: بعض المشايخ
rows.claim: A servant's share in these names is abundant mercy: begin by showing mercy to oneself inwardly and outwardly, then help others attain their needs, guide them, and look on them compassionately.
rows.anchor: وحظ العبد من اسم الرحمن الرحيم أن يكون كثير الرحمة بأن يرحم نفسه أولا ظاهرا وباطنا
